CHALLENGE 004 — TOOL QUICKSTART
A FEW MISSING BYTES / JPEG HEADER REPAIR

Linux (Kali / Ubuntu / WSL2)
----------------------------
Work on a copy of `recovered_photo.bin`.

1. Identify the file:
   file recovered_photo.bin
2. Inspect the first bytes:
   xxd -l 16 recovered_photo.bin
3. The JFIF marker indicates JPEG data. A JPEG begins with FF D8 FF.
4. Replace exactly the first two bytes in a new copy:
   (printf '\xff\xd8'; tail -c +3 recovered_photo.bin) > restored.jpg
5. Verify:
   file restored.jpg
   xxd -l 4 restored.jpg

Windows (HxD)
-------------
1. Open a COPY of `recovered_photo.bin` in HxD: https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/
2. At offset `00000000`, select the first TWO bytes.
3. Use overwrite mode and replace those bytes with `FF D8`. Do not insert bytes.
4. Save the copy as `restored.jpg`.
5. Confirm the first four bytes are `FF D8 FF E0`, then open the image.

Only the first two bytes should change. Preserve the original evidence file.
